decisions.reason: The same-message MODIFY already limits future Transak mints to the active replacement contract, so no additional or corrected Event is needed.
The same-message MODIFY already limits the USDC mint flow to the active replacement contract.
The same-message MODIFY already records that active-system metadata covers only replacement-contract NFTs and excludes legacy-contract metadata.
The same-message MODIFY already excludes legacy-contract NFTs from active ownership and mint reporting.
The same-message MODIFY already restricts dashboard rendering to NFTs from the active replacement contract and excludes legacy-contract NFTs.
The same-message MODIFY already restricts active owner discovery to replacement-contract NFTs and marks legacy-contract NFTs as undiscoverable in the active system.
Selecting the replacement contract does not change the established $30 mint price or revenue-allocation rules.
The replacement-contract decision does not require any change to the current About-page content.
The rule that success feedback appears only after a confirmed mint remains valid unchanged regardless of the active contract.

The replacement-contract scope decision does not alter the approved ETH pricing, exact-output, refund, or insufficient-input behavior; the same-message Event in this Requirement addresses a separate accepted rule.
Changing the active mint contract does not alter which payment options must be displayed or how customers select them.
The active ETH mint path must use the replacement contract because the client accepted excluding old-contract NFTs from the active systems, and no matching Event currently records that restriction.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Despite the lost copies in the old contract, which don't worry me much, I think proceeding this way would be best.
